summary.headline: Kalpataru Q4 FY26 revenue rose to INR 1,694 crore (~3x YoY) on handovers; FY26 pre-sales INR 5,280 crore, up 17%, with no formal FY27 guidance yet.
summary.overview: Q4 FY26 was driven by delivery-led revenue recognition, with 1.37 million sq ft of occupation certificates (OCs) pulling revenue from completed newer projects into the quarter. Q4 pre-sales hit a record INR 1,833 crore (+6% YoY) and collections a record INR 1,487 crore (+41%). FY26 collections grew 34% to INR 4,960 crore, and net debt was INR 8,106 crore (net debt-to-equity about 2x). Management withheld formal FY27 guidance, saying it will come later, but said net debt will not rise in FY27 and debt-to-equity will be below 2x.

financial_highlights.change: nearly 3x vs INR 601 crore in Q4 FY25
management also cited 36% margin for full year; figures as stated on call

financial_highlights.value: INR 1,002 crore (100% basis about INR 1,500 crore)

segments.name: MMR (Mumbai Metro Region)
segments.commentary: 15 ongoing projects with expected inflows of about INR 23,500 crore, the largest contributor. Premium projects include Kalpataru One (Worli), Amare (Juhu), Advay (Borivali), Kalpataru Prive and Azuro (South Mumbai).

segments.name: Pune and other markets
segments.commentary: Together expected to contribute about INR 3,500 crore of inflows from ongoing projects. Kalpataru Blossoms (Pune) may launch in two phases. Hyderabad has one project, described as performing well.

guidance_outlook: No formal FY27 guidance yet; management said it will be issued at a later date, citing macro conditions.
FY27 delivery target of about 5.5 million sq ft; visibility on cash flows for the next 12 months.
FY27 new launches of about 5 million sq ft, GDV about INR 7,800 crore; launch-phase sales target 20-25%; expected FY27 launch sales INR 1,800-2,000 crore.
Net debt to stay at or below the March 2026 level of INR 8,100 crore in FY27, with a marginal absolute reduction targeted; debt-to-equity to be below 2x.

Further refinancing of about INR 1,300 crore expected in the coming quarter, following about INR 3,500 crore refinanced since listing (120 bps lower blended cost of debt, about INR 125 crore annual savings).
Margins on new launches: 20-25% at revenue level and 25-30% on a cash basis, as land payments are largely done.
capex_capacity: Ongoing projects: 20 projects, about 24 million sq ft saleable area, about 11.4 million sq ft already sold; GDV nearly INR 36,000 crore; future inflows about INR 27,000 crore.
FY26 completions: 5.15 million sq ft, about double the prior year; OCs for about 3,000 units. Q4 OCs of about 1.37 million sq ft across six Vivant towers, one Elitus tower and one Aria phase.
FY26 launches: four tower phases in three projects (Eternia, Aria, Shristi Namaah) plus Estella, totalling 1.8 million sq ft. Some launches slipped to H1 FY27 pending approvals.
New BD: redevelopment of Shri Mahalakshmi CHS, Andheri West, about 3 acres, about 0.4 million sq ft carpet area, GDV about INR 1,400 crore.
Construction cost FY26: INR 1,916 crore at 100% level; Kalpataru share INR 1,512 crore. Projects are fully financially closed.
Portfolio: 31 projects, 43 million sq ft saleable area; total future inflows about INR 57,000 crore including RTM and upcoming launches.
demand_pricing: Q4 footfalls and walk-ins described as good, with April also robust; barring an April vacation period and a geopolitical slowdown, no drastic change seen.
Worli (Kalpataru One) sold about INR 400 crore in Q4 FY26, out of about INR 1,000 crore total company sales in March. Management described payment plans as an organic demand driver, not a sales push.
Management said no payment-linked plans are planned for new launches; these are typically offered later in a project's life cycle.
Construction cost inflation of 2-4% attributed to the Middle East crisis, with tile and pipe supply issues resolved; management expects no material impact on sales value.
Management says work-from-home policy should not materially affect MMR demand.

qa_highlights.question: How much of the FY27 launch pipeline (around INR 8,000 crore GDV) will be launched and sold in the year?
qa_highlights.answer: Launches spread through the year, with about three in H1 and the rest in H2 (Kalpataru Blossoms may be phased). Target 20-25% sales at launch, implying about INR 1,800-2,000 crore for FY27.

qa_highlights.question: How much unsold inventory is there, and how long to sell it?
qa_highlights.answer: Unsold inventory in ongoing projects is about INR 22,000 crore, rising to about INR 30,000 crore with another INR 7,000-8,000 crore added in the year. Most should be liquidated over four to five years, with a remainder in a sixth year.

qa_highlights.question: What are the net debt and debt-to-equity targets for the next 12 months?
qa_highlights.answer: Net debt not to exceed the March 2026 level of INR 8,100 crore, with a marginal absolute reduction. Debt-to-equity to be below 2x, with formal guidance to follow.

qa_highlights.question: Where did FY26 operating cash flow go?
qa_highlights.answer: OCF was INR 1,002 crore proportionate (about INR 1,282 crore before INR 280 crore of BD spend on projects acquired after April 2025). Interest and tax were paid from OCF, and debt was reduced by about INR 1,200 crore over the last nine months.

qa_highlights.question: How much cash is locked in RERA accounts?
qa_highlights.answer: Not more than 20% of the INR 1,062 crore closing cash balance is locked in RERA accounts; the rest is free for projects.

qa_highlights.question: What margins are expected on new launches and the INR 28,000 crore forthcoming pipeline?
qa_highlights.answer: Revenue-level margins of 20-25%, with cash margins of 25-30% because land acquisition payments are largely done. Management said nothing further is needed for the pipeline, with project-level capex data to follow offline.

risks_watch: No formal FY27 guidance yet; management will issue it later.

Q4 revenue and profit were lifted by OC-linked recognition of completed newer projects, so quarterly earnings may be lumpy. Full-year PAT was only INR 80 crore against INR 1,022 crore adjusted EBITDA.
Net debt of INR 8,106 crore with about 2x debt-to-equity, and some BD investment planned in FY27.
Some FY26 launches slipped to H1 FY27 pending regulatory approvals.
Middle East geopolitical situation, construction cost inflation of 2-4%, and footfall conversion in the coming months.
Next quarter: refinancing of about INR 1,300 crore and the FY27 guidance release.
summary.management_tone: Confident on execution, delivery and cash collection, and on sales momentum in MMR. Cautious and non-committal on forward numbers: FY27 guidance, the debt-reduction path and project-level cost data were all deferred to later disclosure.
key_quotes: Our momentum peaked in the 4th Quarter, where we achieved our highest ever quarterly pre-sales of INR 1,833 crores.

The robust Q4 performance is directly linked to these newer projects reaching the handover stage, and we expect this delivery-led revenue recognition to be a recurring phenomenon in our financial narrative going forward.
We are not chasing volume for the sake of scale.
